title: Low-Sensitivity In Vivo Nuclei
summary: Three of these nuclei have genuinely been imaged in living humans: 7Li in the brains of patients on lithium carbonate at 3T, 4T and 7T; 39K in calf and thigh muscle and brain at 7T and 9.4T; and 35Cl in brain and muscle at 7T. The rest have not, and the arithmetic says why: receptivity alone is not the problem, it is receptivity multiplied by the concentration the nucleus actually reaches in tissue. 7Li has 0.27 of the 1H receptivity, three times that of 23Na, but sits at only 0.3 to 0.9 mM in brain; 39K sits at 80 mM in muscle but has 1/194 of the 23Na receptivity; 25Mg and 43Ca lose on both counts at once, and 43Ca is 213000 times weaker in vivo than 23Na even before the quadrupolar linewidth is counted. 14N is broadened out of existence except at high-symmetry sites, and 15N is only useful hyperpolarized, where its low gyromagnetic ratio stops being a liability and becomes the reason its polarization survives for minutes.

facts.label: Receptivity at natural abundance, relative to 1H
facts.note: Computed as abundance x |gamma/gamma_H|^3 x I(I+1)/(3/4); relative to 13C these are 7Li 1593, 87Rb 289, 133Cs 283, 35Cl 21.0, 14N 5.90, 39K 2.79, 25Mg 1.58, 43Ca 0.051, 15N 0.022, which match the standard tables.

facts.label: Receptivity times tissue concentration, the number that decides feasibility
facts.value: Relative to 23Na at 40 mM: 31P at 30 mM is 0.54; 7Li at 0.5 mM is 0.037; 35Cl at 12 mM is 0.012; 39K at 83 mM is 0.011; 14N at a 10 mM site is 2.7e-3; 25Mg at 10 mM total Mg is 7.2e-4; 43Ca at 2 mM total Ca is 4.7e-6
facts.note: Against tissue water 1H at about 80 M the same numbers read 1/22000 for 23Na, 1/590000 for 7Li, 1/1.9e6 for 35Cl, 1/2.0e6 for 39K, 1/3.0e7 for 25Mg and 1/4.6e9 for 43Ca; anything past about 1/2e6 needs 7T or above and a voxel of order 1 mL.

facts.label: Larmor frequencies and the hardware they demand
facts.value: At 7T: 7Li 115.8 MHz, 87Rb 97.9 MHz, 23Na 78.8 MHz, 133Cs 39.3 MHz, 15N 30.2 MHz, 35Cl 29.2 MHz, 14N 21.5 MHz, 43Ca 20.1 MHz, 25Mg 18.3 MHz, 39K 13.9 MHz. At 3T: 7Li 49.6 MHz, 39K 5.97 MHz, 35Cl 12.5 MHz
facts.note: 39K at 13.9 MHz falls below the tuning range of most commercial 7T X-nucleus chains; the first human 39K images were acquired by down-converting the scanner's 7Li channel at 115 MHz to 14 MHz with a custom frequency converter.

facts.label: 7Li in human brain, the one real clinical application
facts.value: Brain-to-serum ratio 0.52 +/- 0.16 at 3T with ISIS (brain 0.35 +/- 0.11 mEq/L, serum 0.69 +/- 0.19 mEq/L); 0.39 +/- 0.08 whole brain and 0.92 +/- 0.16 at the local maximum by 3D MRSI at 4T; brain equals 0.40 x plasma at 7T with a UTE non-Cartesian readout in 21 patients, R = 0.74
facts.note: The whole-brain ratio clusters near 0.4 to 0.5 across three fields and three sequences, but the distribution is not uniform, so a single whole-brain ratio hides a factor of two between regions; at 7T the left hippocampus stood out consistently across the cohort.

facts.label: 7Li acquisition that works on a clinical 3T
facts.value: 3D balanced SSFP, TR 9.4 ms, TE 4.5 ms, flip 60 degrees, 500 averages, reconstructed 15 x 15 x 25 mm, 8 minutes, dual-tuned 1H/7Li birdcage; three times the in-brain signal of spoiled gradient echo at equal scan time, and the spoiled version failed to give usable images in 3 of 4 subjects even at 24 minutes
facts.note: The matched SPGR comparison ran the Ernst angle at 4.6 degrees for TR 6.7 ms, which implies a 7Li T1 near 2.1 s in vivo; a long T1 and a singlet resonance is exactly the case where bSSFP beats a spoiled sequence, and it is why 7Li imaging does not need ultra-high field.

facts.label: 7Li relaxation and compartmentation
facts.value: Rat brain at 7T, biexponential T2: 14.8 +/- 4.3 ms assigned intracellular and 295 +/- 61 ms assigned extracellular; intracellular fraction 54.5 +/- 6.7 percent of total brain lithium, range 37.3 to 64.8 percent
facts.note: 7Li has the second smallest quadrupole moment of the alkali metals at -4.01 fm^2, a factor of 2.6 below 23Na's +10.4 fm^2 and so about seven times gentler in quadrupolar relaxation rate, which is why its T2 is measured in tens to hundreds of ms rather than a few ms; that is what makes a conventional gradient echo or spin echo viable at all.

facts.label: 39K in human muscle, quantified
facts.value: Fat-corrected apparent tissue potassium 83.2 mM (IQR 22.3) in healthy calf at 7T; 79.1 +/- 10.0 mM in a separate control group; 72.7 +/- 6.8 mM in primary aldosteronism, rising to 80.9 +/- 9.8 mM after mineralocorticoid receptor blockade or adrenalectomy; near zero, 4.3 mM (IQR 2.7), in muscle with fat fraction above 80 percent
facts.note: About 98 percent of body potassium is intracellular and skeletal muscle holds roughly 75 percent of the total, so a tissue potassium map is close to an intracellular volume map; serum potassium did not correlate with baseline aTPC in the aldosteronism cohort, which is the point of measuring it.

facts.label: 39K relaxation and the cost of every microsecond of TE
facts.value: Muscle T2*fast 1.2 ms and T2*slow 8.1 ms; by lineshape fitting at 7T, head T2*fast 0.51 +/- 0.01 ms and T2*slow 6.21 +/- 0.05 ms, thigh satellites 1.56 and 1.42 ms with a 9.67 +/- 0.04 ms centre line; quadrupolar satellites shifted about 200 Hz with the calf parallel to B0
facts.note: With 60 percent at 1.2 ms and 40 percent at 8.1 ms, TE 0.4 ms retains 81 percent of the muscle signal, TE 1 ms retains 61 percent and TE 2 ms retains 43 percent; the residual quadrupolar splitting also means a single Lorentzian fit is wrong and the FID oscillates.

facts.label: What 39K costs in voxel volume
facts.value: 7T density-adapted 3D radial, 39K TR 40 ms, TE 0.4 ms, 90 degrees, 2960 projections, 5 ms readout, 8 x 8 x 32 mm (2.05 mL), 9 min 52 s; the 23Na scan in the same session ran 2.5 x 2.5 x 15 mm (0.094 mL) in 10 min 46 s
facts.note: Same subject, same coil, essentially the same time: the 39K voxel is 22 times the volume of the 23Na voxel, which is the 194-fold receptivity deficit converted into geometry. Brain 39K has been done at 9.5 mm isotropic in 30 min at 7T and at 9.4T.

facts.label: 35Cl in human brain and muscle at 7T
facts.value: T1 9.2 ms in brain and 4.0 +/- 0.7 ms in muscle (monoexponential fits); partial-volume-corrected T2* long/short 8.9 +/- 1.4 / 1.0 +/- 0.4 ms in grey matter and 5.9 +/- 0.3 / 0.4 +/- 0.1 ms in white matter; brain at (6 mm)^3 in 9 min 45 s, muscle at (11 mm)^3 in 35 min; 15-fold lower phantom SNR than 23Na
facts.note: Per nucleus 35Cl is 26 times less receptive than 23Na, and its T2* is about four times shorter, so the practical rule is a 6 mm voxel where sodium gets 3 mm. Glioblastoma showed raised Cl- and raised inversion-recovery Cl- signal; hypokalaemic periodic paralysis raised both Cl- and Na+ in calf.

facts.label: 35Cl concentrations to calibrate against
facts.value: Serum chloride 98 to 107 mM and CSF chloride 118 to 132 mM by clinical assay; apparent tissue chloride near 12 mM in normal calf muscle at 7T, against about 36 mM in an enchondroma (a threefold elevation, alongside a thirteenfold sodium elevation)
facts.note: Mature neurons hold intracellular Cl- at roughly 5 to 10 mM against 100 to 120 mM outside, so like 23Na the tissue-average signal is dominated by the small extracellular compartment and moves when the extracellular volume fraction moves.

facts.label: 25Mg and 43Ca, and why nobody has done them in a person
facts.value: 25Mg is 10.00 percent abundant, spin 5/2, gamma -2.608 MHz/T, Q 19.94 fm^2 (the largest here); 43Ca is 0.135 percent abundant, spin 7/2, gamma -2.870 MHz/T. Cytosolic free Mg2+ measured by 31P is 0.45 to 0.76 mM in skeletal muscle, against about 0.18 mM reported for human occipital lobe; resting cytosolic free Ca2+ is about 100 nM with total soft-tissue calcium of order 1 to 2 mM
facts.note: Even at 100 percent 43Ca enrichment and 2 mM total calcium the in vivo signal is only 0.35 percent of 23Na's, and the fraction that is free rather than protein- or membrane-bound is a few parts in 10000; 25Mg carries the biggest quadrupole moment in this set, so the bound pool that carries most of the magnesium is broadened to invisibility. Free Mg2+ in humans is obtained from the 31P ATP chemical shifts instead.

facts.label: 43Ca in bone is a linewidth problem, not a concentration problem
facts.value: Cortical bone mineral holds calcium at of order 10 mol/L, which at 0.135 percent abundance gives a raw receptivity comparable to 0.5 mM 7Li in brain
facts.note: The signal is nonetheless unobservable in a scanner because the rigid hydroxyapatite lattice spreads it over a quadrupolar powder pattern; 43Ca work on calcium phosphates needs isotopic enrichment plus magic angle spinning with DNP, which has no in vivo counterpart.

facts.label: 87Rb and 133Cs as potassium congeners
facts.value: 87Rb: spin 3/2, 27.83 percent abundant, gamma 13.98 MHz/T, receptivity 0.049 of 1H, Q 13.35 fm^2 (larger than 23Na's 10.4). 133Cs: spin 7/2, 100 percent abundant, gamma 5.612 MHz/T, receptivity 0.048 of 1H, Q -0.343 fm^2, the smallest of any alkali
facts.note: Both are about half as receptive as 23Na, so sensitivity is not the obstacle; the obstacle is that you have to put the ion into the subject. 87Rb work is isolated perfused rat and pig heart, kidney, muscle, salivary gland and red cells, where intracellular Rb+/K+ partitioning is about 20:1 and Rb+ uptake is 80 percent ouabain-sensitive. 133Cs in rats reaches a brain-to-CSF ratio of 9:1 and a muscle-to-plasma ratio of 40:1, about 40-fold and 360-fold intracellular-to-extracellular content, but CsCl is cardiotoxic in humans and rubidium clears over weeks, so the human potassium-analogue tracer is 82Rb PET with its 75 s half-life, not 87Rb MR.

facts.label: 14N versus 15N, and hyperpolarized 15N as a storage nucleus
facts.value: 14N: spin 1, 99.636 percent abundant, receptivity 5.9 times 13C, Q 2.044 fm^2. 15N: spin 1/2, 0.364 percent abundant, receptivity 0.022 times 13C, gamma -4.317 MHz/T. Thermal 15N polarization at 3T and 310 K is 1.0 ppm against 9.9 ppm for 1H
facts.note: 14N is abundant and not badly receptive but only nuclei in near-tetrahedral sites give usable lines: NH4+, urea, and the trimethylammonium head groups that reach about 90 mM in renal inner medulla in rat, while amide and amine nitrogen is broadened by kHz or more. 15N is the mirror image, clean spin 1/2 with a 900 ppm shift range and negligible abundance, so it is only useful hyperpolarized.

facts.label: Hyperpolarized 15N lifetimes and polarizations
facts.value: dDNP on 1-15N-nicotinamide reached 13.0 +/- 1.9 percent polarization with T1 41 s at pH 12 and 1 T, falling to a few seconds at neutral pH below 1 T. SABRE-SHEATH on 15N2-diazirine gave magnetization decay of 5.8 min and singlet-order decay of 23 min with signal detectable beyond an hour. A 15N2-diazirine-tagged GGT substrate had T1 196 s and its product 81 s at 1 T, with a 6.3 ppm substrate-product shift, imaged in rat kidney on a clinical 3T scanner. Parahydrogen-polarized 15N pyridine N-oxides reached 47 percent with T1 up to 477 s
facts.note: Dipolar and CSA relaxation both scale as gamma^2, so the low 15N gyromagnetic ratio that ruins its thermal sensitivity is what buys minutes of lifetime at a quaternary or otherwise proton-remote nitrogen. Against natural-abundance thermal 15N at 3T, 20 percent polarization plus full enrichment is a gain of about 5e7.

practice: Do the concentration times receptivity product before you book magnet time. Receptivity alone is misleading: 7Li beats 39K by a factor of 570 per nucleus but only by a factor of 3.4 in vivo, because lithium sits at 0.5 mM and potassium at 83 mM.

For 7Li stay on 3T and use balanced SSFP rather than chasing a 7T slot. T1 near 2 s and a single narrow line is the bSSFP best case; it gave three times the SPGR signal at matched time, and 25 mm isotropic in 8 minutes on a clinical scanner is enough to see regional heterogeneity.

For 39K and 35Cl use a density-adapted 3D radial or twisted projection readout with TE at or below 0.4 ms and a short readout. A 5 to 10 ms readout is already a strong T2* filter on outer k-space when the fast component is 0.5 to 1.2 ms, so nominal resolution overstates what you resolve.

Set TR from the short T1, not from habit. 35Cl T1 is 9.2 ms in brain and 4.0 ms in muscle, and 39K T1 is of order 10 to 20 ms, so a 90 degree hard pulse at TR 40 to 65 ms is at or near the Ernst optimum and the SAR headroom at 14 to 29 MHz is enormous. Gradient duty cycle, not power deposition, will stop you.

Put multi-compartment reference phantoms in the field of view and bracket the expected range. The Erlangen 39K/23Na protocol used five vials spanning [Na]/[K] of 10/240 to 40/120 mM; a single-point calibration cannot absorb the relaxation and partial-volume corrections these nuclei need.

At 39K's 13.9 MHz you are coil-noise dominated, not sample-noise dominated, so SNR scales closer to B0^(7/4) than B0. Moving 39K from 7T to 9.4T is worth more than the field ratio suggests; moving 7Li from 3T to 7T, where you are sample-dominated, is worth much less.

For 15N, hyperpolarize a nitrogen with no directly bonded proton and no large CSA. Diazirines, N-oxides and quaternary ammoniums are the shapes that give minutes; an amine or amide 15N will relax in seconds and you will have built a 13C tracer with none of 13C's advantages.

Measure free Mg2+ from the 31P ATP chemical shifts and free Ca2+ with an optical or fluorine indicator. There is no route to either from 25Mg or 43Ca in a person, and pretending otherwise burns a grant.
pitfalls: Quoting a whole-brain lithium concentration or a single brain-to-serum ratio. The distribution is heterogeneous in every study that had the resolution to see it, with a coefficient of variation near 28 percent within brain and a local maximum roughly twice the whole-brain mean, so a scalar ratio averages away the thing you scanned for.

Treating apparent tissue potassium as intracellular potassium without a fat fraction correction. Potassium in adipose tissue is close to zero, so in fat-replaced muscle the uncorrected aTPC tracks fat content rather than cell health; the fat-corrected value is what separates disease from replacement, and the correction becomes numerically unstable above about 60 percent fat fraction.

Fitting a single exponential to 39K or 35Cl decay. Both are biexponential, the 39K FID additionally oscillates from residual quadrupolar splitting with satellites shifted by roughly 200 Hz in muscle parallel to B0, and the apparent T2* you extract from a monoexponential fit depends entirely on which echoes you sampled.

Assuming the reference phantom relaxes like tissue. A saline or gel standard with a monoexponential T2* of tens of ms will not track a tissue signal whose fast component is 0.4 to 1.2 ms, so the concentration scale drifts with TE and the error is systematic, not random.

Shimming the X-nucleus on a 1H map, or forgetting there is no 1H channel at all. Dual-tuned 23Na/39K birdcages often have no proton channel, so shimming has to be done on the 23Na signal itself, and the coil swap between the X-nucleus and 1H scans deforms the limb enough to break the co-registration that the partial volume correction depends on.

Reading a low 43Ca or 25Mg receptivity number and concluding that a bigger magnet or a longer scan will fix it. For 43Ca the free ion is at 100 nM and the abundant pool is bound and quadrupolar-broadened; there is no field strength and no averaging time at which the free calcium becomes visible.
